title: Custom Logo Printing
description: Screen print, heat transfer, and embroidery options for branded evaporative cooler covers — file specs, colors, and volume pricing for contractors and property managers.

sections.heading: Printing Methods
sections.body: Screen printing suits solid spot colors and larger production runs. Heat transfer handles full-color logos on polyester bases. Embroidery adds premium texture on 600D and canvas covers but is limited by panel thickness and seam placement.
bullets: Screen print: economical at 50+ units, excellent fade resistance on UV-rated inks
Heat transfer: full-color logos, ideal for property management branding
Embroidery: high-end contractor branding on chest-panel placements
Single-color logo often included on commercial orders of 50+ units — confirm at quote

sections.heading: File Requirements
sections.body: Supply vector art when possible (AI, EPS, PDF with outlined fonts). Minimum 300 DPI raster art at final print size for heat transfer. Specify print width in inches and placement (front panel, top, or wrap band).
bullets: Vector preferred: AI, EPS, SVG, or PDF (outlined)
Raster: PNG or TIFF, 300 DPI at print dimensions
Indicate PMS colors for brand matching
We provide a digital mockup before production on new artwork

sections.heading: Color Options
sections.body: Match corporate palettes using Pantone references on white, gray, beige, navy, or charcoal cover stock. Dark covers may need an underbase for bright logos. Reflective silver and white tops are popular on rooftop units in hot climates.
bullets: Standard cover colors: gray, beige, navy, charcoal, black, silver
Custom dye-matched fabric available on volume orders
Light logos on dark fabric may need white underbase — affects hand-feel slightly
UV-resistant inks recommended for all outdoor placements

sections.heading: Pricing
sections.body: Logo pricing depends on print size, color count, method, and quantity. A single-color chest logo on a standard residential cover differs from a full-wrap multi-color industrial panel. Volume tiers start around 25–50 units for meaningful per-unit discounts.
bullets: One-color screen: lowest cost per unit at volume
Full-color transfer: higher setup, best for complex logos
Setup fees amortize across reorders using stored screens or digital files
Request a bundled quote: covers + printing + shipping to your warehouse

intro: Branded covers turn equipment protection into on-site marketing for HVAC contractors, hotels, and facility management companies. Logo printing is available on most cover types and materials, with methods chosen based on color count, durability needs, and order quantity.

title: Custom Cover Materials
description: Select the right fabric, coating, and lining for your custom evaporative cooler cover — with sample options and performance ratings for B2B orders.

sections.heading: Material Selection
sections.body: Start with environment: desert sun → UV-stabilized 600D or reflective silver topcoat; coastal salt air → heavier PU or TPU lamination; heavy rain → PVC-backed or fully sealed vinyl; winter off-season → insulated laminate. Indoor or warehouse storage may only need 300D polyester.
bullets: 600D Oxford + PU: default for most custom residential and light commercial jobs
900D + TPU: industrial and extra-large cabinets
300D + PVC backing: maximum waterproofing at moderate weight
Mesh: in-season pest and debris barrier — not a winter solution

sections.heading: Material Samples
sections.body: For repeat B2B buyers and new commercial accounts, we can ship swatches of shortlisted fabrics before production. Samples help facilities teams approve color, stiffness, and coating hand-feel for brand guidelines.
bullets: Request swatches when specifying a new material code for the first time
Include your climate zone and installation type (rooftop, wall, window)
Logo printing samples available on 600D and vinyl bases
Note fire-retardant or chemical-resistant requirements at quote stage

sections.heading: Performance Ratings
sections.body: Compare materials on waterproof rating (mm H₂O), UV stability, abrasion resistance, and operating temperature — not denier alone. A 600D UV-stabilized fabric often outlasts untreated 900D in direct sun.
bullets: Water-resistant (PU): sheds rain and dust; breathable hem recommended
Waterproof (sealed seams + PVC): for standing water and snow load regions
UPF 50+ coatings: for rooftop and southwest exposure
Insulated (foam core): freeze protection and draft blocking in winter

intro: Custom orders let you pair fabric weight, coatings, and colors to each job site. Contractors often standardize on one 600D PU spec across a fleet while specifying 900D or vinyl for exposed rooftops. We can hold the same material code across reorders for multi-property maintenance programs.

title: Custom Opening Design
description: Ventilation cutouts, service panels, and duct openings for side-draft and down-draft cooler covers — designed to your cabinet layout.

sections.heading: Opening Types
sections.body: Common openings include screened vents (mesh-backed), zippered access flaps, split corners for electrical boxes, grommeted drain points, and full perimeter drop skirts for units mounted on curbs.
bullets: Screened vents: reduce condensation while blocking debris
Zippered panels: service access without removing the entire cover
Grommets: drainage and tie-down anchor points
Split corner: clears exterior disconnect boxes on commercial side-draft units

sections.heading: Side Draft Openings
sections.body: Wall-mounted side-draft coolers often need low-side clearance for water lines and high-side relief for warm air paths. Mark pipe exits on your dimension sheet; we position openings away from prevailing wind when possible.
bullets: Keep water line cutouts above typical splash height
Reinforce edges with binding tape on high-wear openings
Match opening to pad frame — not only to outer cabinet line
Browse side-draft cooler covers for standard configurations

sections.heading: Down Draft Openings
sections.body: Rooftop down-draft units may need top ventilation or skirt clearance around the curb. Specify if the cover must clear a crane lift lid or maintenance hatch. Drainage openings prevent water weight from collapsing lightweight tops.
bullets: Top panel: reflective or reinforced depending on sun load
Curb-mounted units: measure curb OD separately from cabinet OD
Wind exposure: fewer large openings on prevailing-wind side
See down-draft product category for rooftop-ready features

sections.heading: Custom Configurations
sections.body: Send a sketch or annotated photos for unusual layouts — dual ducts, offset motors, or combined cooler + heat exchanger cabinets. We engineer one-off patterns and can replicate approved designs on future reorders by pattern ID.
bullets: Pattern ID stored for repeat commercial orders
Multiple openings per face allowed with reinforced seams
Velcro, zipper, or laced closure per opening — specify access frequency
Request a quote with photos for complex layouts

intro: A cover that blocks required airflow or traps heat can damage pads and motors. Opening design balances protection with function: screened vents for off-season breathing, zippered panels for service access, and reinforced hems around cutouts so fabric does not tear at stress points.

title: Custom Cover Sizes
description: Order evaporative cooler covers in any dimension — submission format, size limits, and solutions for irregular cabinets and mixed fleets.

sections.heading: Submitting Dimensions
sections.body: Email or quote form: company name, quantity, material preference, and a dimension table per unit model. One row per unique size; attach photos if the shape is non-rectangular. We confirm slack policy (typically +1–2 in. on width and depth) before cutting.
bullets: Format: Model name | Width | Depth | Height | Notes (openings, color)
Photos of all four sides reduce back-and-forth
Bulk CSV/spreadsheet accepted for 25+ unit mixed-size orders
Pre-production sample may be available for a qualifying order before full production

sections.heading: Minimum and Maximum Sizes
sections.body: We produce patterns for small window units through large industrial evaporative coolers exceeding 50 in. per side. Extremely compact or oversized units may require reinforced panels or panelized construction — flagged at quote review.
bullets: Small window units: often 20–30 in. per side — specify frame overlap needs
Standard residential: 28–42 in. footprints most common
Commercial / industrial: 45–60+ in. — reinforced stress points included
Flexible low MOQ confirmed from dimensions, material, quantity, printing, destination, and shipping method

sections.heading: Irregular Shapes
sections.body: Round cylinders, tapered hoods, and offset duct bumps are common on older swamp coolers. We flat-pattern or segment covers with darts, gussets, or zippered access panels so the fabric does not fight the geometry.
bullets: Round: provide diameter at the widest point plus straight-side height
Offset vents: mark XY position from a consistent corner on your photo
Split corners for junction boxes — specify side and height from base
See opening design options for duct and service panel cutouts

intro: Every cooler model has a unique cabinet outline. Custom sizing removes the guesswork of one-size-fits-all retail covers. Send outside W×D×H dimensions (or diameter × height for round units) and we cut patterns with appropriate slack, hem style, and tie-down placement.

title: Cooler Cover Materials Guide
description: Compare polyester, canvas, vinyl, mesh, and insulated fabrics for evaporative cooler covers — and choose the right material for your climate and installation.

sections.heading: Polyester (300D–900D Oxford)
sections.body: Polyester is the most common cooler-cover fabric because it balances cost, weight, and weather resistance. Denier (D) indicates thread thickness: 300D is lighter and suited to sheltered installs; 600D is the industry workhorse for residential and light commercial units; 900D canvas-style polyester handles large spans and rooftop exposure.
bullets: PU (polyurethane) coating: water-resistant, good for most dry and mixed climates
UV stabilizers: essential for rooftop and desert sun — pair with our UV-shield products for direct exposure
Typical weight: 0.8–2.0 kg depending on size and denier
Best for: side-draft, down-draft, and standard custom covers where you need durability without vinyl stiffness

sections.heading: Canvas
sections.body: Canvas covers use a heavier woven base (often cotton-poly blend or polyester canvas) with a rugged hand-feel. They resist abrasion and punctures better than light polyester, which matters on industrial sites and rooftop units with sharp flashing or gravel.
bullets: Heavier than 600D polyester — plan for stronger tie-downs on large covers
Often paired with PU or wax-style treatments for water resistance (not fully waterproof without lamination)
Popular on commercial and extra-large cooler covers
Allow extra drying time after rain before storage to prevent mildew on natural-fiber blends

sections.heading: Vinyl & PVC-Backed Fabrics
sections.body: Vinyl and PVC-backed polyester deliver the highest rain protection. Sealed seams and a waterproof rating (e.g. 5000 mm hydrostatic head) keep water out of pads and cabinets during off-season storage. These fabrics are stiffer and louder in wind than oxford polyester.
bullets: Ideal for heavy-rain regions and units left covered through wet seasons
PVC backing adds stiffness — specify split corners or zippers if you need access to disconnect boxes
Anti-mildew treatments recommended for humid climates
See our waterproof premium cover line for fully sealed construction

sections.heading: Mesh
sections.body: High-density polyester mesh blocks leaves, dust, and pests while allowing airflow. Mesh is not a winter cover — use it in-season or in mild climates where condensation under a solid cover is a concern.
bullets: Typical mesh aperture: ~1 mm for debris filtration without starving airflow
Ultra-light (0.3–0.6 kg) — easy on/off during operating season
Pairs well with solid winter covers: mesh in summer, insulated or solid cover in winter
Browse mesh cooler covers for breathable protection options

sections.heading: Insulated Materials
sections.body: Insulated covers add a foam or thermal lining (commonly 3–5 mm) to reduce freeze risk, block drafts, and slow temperature swing inside the cabinet. They are thicker and need slightly larger clearances than uninsulated covers.
bullets: Recommended for winter storage and cold-climate off-season protection
Condensation management: ensure the unit is dry before covering; vented hem designs help
Heavier than standard polyester — use reinforced corners on rooftop units
Compare insulated vs. mesh vs. solid covers in our material comparison blog

intro: Fabric choice drives waterproofing, UV resistance, weight, and lifespan. Most swamp cooler and evaporative cooler covers use coated polyester (300D–900D), canvas, vinyl-backed fabrics, breathable mesh, or insulated laminates. Use this guide to match material to how and where your unit runs.

title: Cooler Cover Installation Guide
description: How to install evaporative and swamp cooler covers on wall-mount, rooftop, and window units — including wind tie-down and safety checks.

sections.heading: Pre-Installation Checklist
sections.body: Confirm the cooler is off, water drained, and pads are dry. Remove debris from the cabinet top and verify your cover orientation (tagged front/back if applicable). Inspect tie-down straps, drawcords, and grommets before climbing to a rooftop unit.
bullets: Power off at disconnect — never cover a running unit
Drain pan and water lines; dry 24 hours minimum
Clear leaves and grit from the cabinet top
Lay out cover and identify front, back, and opening alignment

sections.heading: Basic Installation Steps
sections.body: Drape the cover over the cabinet starting from the highest point on down-draft units (or from the back on side-draft wall units). Pull the hem evenly around all sides before tightening. Secure the elastic hem or drawcord last so fabric seats flat without twisting.
bullets: Down-draft: align top panel first, then pull skirt down over corners
Side-draft: fit over top, then work hem under bottom flange
Zippered openings: close zippers after hem is positioned
Stand back and check for bunched fabric that can hold water

sections.heading: Rooftop Installation
sections.body: Use fall protection and a helper when possible. Route tie-downs to structural anchors — not loose conduit or pipe straps. Corner webbing on rooftop-grade covers accepts bungee or ratchet straps; avoid overtightening which can tear grommets.
bullets: OSHA-compliant ladder and harness for roof work
Four-point tie-down in high-wind zones
Reflective top panel faces up — verify orientation
Do not trap standing water — confirm drainage grommets are open

sections.heading: Securing in High Winds
sections.body: In sustained winds above 40 mph (64 km/h), use all provided tie-down points and choose 600D or heavier fabric. Cross straps over the top can supplement corner ties on extra-large covers. Inspect after major storms and retighten when fabric relaxes.
bullets: Ratchet straps preferred over single bungees for large commercial covers
Avoid sharp edges — use corner protectors if straps contact metal flashing
Re-tighten 48 hours after first install — fabric relaxes initially
Remove cover before high-wind events if not rated for your exposure class

intro: Proper installation keeps covers in place through wind and weather without stressing seams. Always shut down and disconnect power before covering, drain the reservoir, and let internal components dry 24 hours to prevent mildew under the fabric.

title: Cooler Cover Maintenance Guide
description: Clean, store, and repair evaporative cooler covers to extend fabric life — by material type and season.

sections.heading: Regular Cleaning
sections.body: Brush off dry dust monthly during the covered season. Wash once per year (or before off-season storage) with mild soap and cool water — never bleach unless the fabric supplier specifies it. Rinse thoroughly and air-dry fully before folding.
bullets: Polyester / canvas: soft brush + mild detergent, cold water rinse
Vinyl: wipe with damp cloth; avoid petroleum solvents
Mesh: hose down gently; do not machine wash with agitators
Insulated: spot-clean when possible to preserve foam core

sections.heading: Stain Removal
sections.body: Treat bird droppings and sap promptly — they etch coatings if baked in sun. Use a soft cloth and diluted mild detergent; for stubborn marks on vinyl, a dedicated marine/vinyl cleaner is safer than household solvents.
bullets: Act within 48 hours on organic stains
No chlorine bleach on PU-coated polyester
Test cleaner on an inside hem first
Rinse soap residue — it attracts dust when dry

sections.heading: Seasonal Storage
sections.body: Fold loosely along existing creases; do not compress insulated covers under heavy items. Store in a breathable bag or box in a dry, rodent-free space. Silica gel packs help in humid warehouses.
bullets: Ensure cover is 100% dry before bagging
Avoid hot attics above 120°F (49°C) for PVC-backed fabrics
Hang large commercial covers on a rod if folding creases stress seams
Label bag with size and model for faster reinstall next season

sections.heading: Repair Tips
sections.body: Small tears in polyester can be patched with outdoor fabric repair tape or sewn with UV-rated thread. Replace torn grommets rather than pulling straps through ripped holes. Seams showing white PU failure may need professional re-coating or replacement on high-value commercial covers.
bullets: Tape patches: round the corners of patch pieces to prevent peel
Restitch loose hems before they propagate
Replace missing drawcord before wind season
Contact us for bulk repair or replacement on fleet accounts

intro: Covers last longer when cleaned before storage and kept dry between seasons. Mud, bird droppings, and tree sap break down PU coatings over time. Follow material-specific cleaning to avoid stripping waterproof layers or melting heat-transfer logos.

title: How to Measure Your Cooler for a Cover
description: Step-by-step instructions to measure width, depth, and height of your evaporative cooler for a custom-fit cover — including protrusions and rooftop units.

deepDiveLinks.label: What Is an Evaporative Cooler Cover?

sections.heading: Tools Needed
sections.body: A steel tape measure (preferred over cloth), notepad or phone camera, and optionally a helper for large rooftop units. For down-draft coolers, use a ladder with fall protection and measure from the roof deck to the top of the cabinet.
bullets: Tape measure (ft/in or metric)
Camera — photos speed up custom quotes
Ladder and harness for rooftop units
Model nameplate photo (optional but helpful)

sections.heading: Step 1: Measure Width
sections.body: Width is the longest horizontal side of the cabinet footprint, usually the left-to-right dimension when facing the access panel. Measure at the widest point including corner trim — not across the pad opening inside the hood.
bullets: Measure twice at mid-height and near the top in case the cabinet tapers
Include side flanges or motor humps that extend past the main box
Record in inches to the nearest ¼ in. (or mm)

sections.heading: Step 2: Measure Depth
sections.body: Depth is the front-to-back dimension of the exterior cabinet. On side-draft units mounted to a wall, depth is from the wall surface to the outermost point of the cooler housing (not the pad frame only).
bullets: Account for water lines, float valves, and brackets that project beyond the cabinet
If a pipe exits the side, mark its location for a custom opening
Wall-mount units: measure from the wall to the farthest protrusion

sections.heading: Step 3: Measure Height
sections.body: Height runs from the mounting surface (roof curb or wall bracket base) to the highest point of the cabinet — often a vent cap or lift lid. For down-draft units, include the rain collar if it projects above the roof line.
bullets: Do not compress the measurement if a spring-loaded hood rises above the frame
Flat-top units: add note if water pools — we can specify drainage grommets
Round units: measure height on the straight side, then diameter separately

sections.heading: Step 4: Note Protrusions
sections.body: List every item that breaks the rectangular outline: electrical disconnect boxes, side ducts, overflow drains, service panels, and guy-wire anchors. Custom openings or split corners prevent stretched fabric and torn seams.
bullets: Mark disconnect box location (common on side-draft commercial units)
Photograph all four sides — one missing side causes fit issues
Specify if the cover must clear a locked access door
See common sizing mistakes before you submit your quote request

intro: Accurate measurements prevent gaps that let in dust, wind, and rain. Measure the outside of the metal or plastic cabinet — not the pad, not the internal frame. Record width, depth, and height at the widest points, then note any obstructions that need cutouts or extra slack.

title: Cooler Cover Sizes
description: Standard evaporative cooler cover sizes, custom sizing, and how to pick the right fit for side-draft, down-draft, and commercial units.

sections.heading: Standard Size Chart
sections.body: Many residential swamp coolers fall into recurring cabinet footprints. Side-draft and window units often range from roughly 22×18×28 in. up to 40×40×45 in. Down-draft rooftop units commonly run 28×28×29 in. through 38×38×44 in. Commercial and industrial cabinets can exceed 50×50×54 in.
bullets: Side-draft / wall-mount: typically narrower depth, wider width — verify electrical boxes on the exterior
Down-draft / rooftop: allow extra height for vent caps and rain collars
Round / cylindrical units: size by diameter and height, not rectangular W×D×H
Always confirm against your actual measurements — model charts vary by brand and pad thickness

sections.heading: Custom Sizing
sections.body: When your cabinet does not match a standard chart, custom covers are cut to your submitted dimensions. We add controlled slack on width and depth (typically 1–2 in.) unless you specify a compression fit for indoor storage. Height is usually matched closely to avoid pooling rain on flat tops.
bullets: Submit outside dimensions in inches or millimeters — include photos for non-standard shapes
Mixed batch orders: send a spreadsheet of unit sizes for multi-site rollouts
Flexible low MOQ confirmed from size, material, quantity, printing, destination, and shipping method
Production lead time: commonly 10–14 business days after specification approval; transit is separate

sections.heading: How to Choose
sections.body: Match cover type to installation: rooftop down-draft covers need drainage and wind tie-downs; side-draft covers need clearance for wall brackets; window units need frame-friendly hems. If the unit stays outdoors year-round in sun, prioritize UV-rated or reflective top panels over the lightest fabric.
bullets: Between two sizes → size up, then adjust with elastic hem, drawcord, or straps
Units with exterior junction boxes → request split-corner or notch openings
High-wind roofs → choose 600D+ fabric and four-point tie-down
Still unsure? Use our measuring guide or request a quote with your dimensions

intro: Cooler covers are sized by outside cabinet dimensions — width × depth × height — not pad size or model name alone. Manufacturers build in 1–2 inches (25–50 mm) of leeway so covers slide over hardware, pad frames, and minor model variations. When your measurements fall between two sizes, choose the larger cover and tighten with drawcord or straps.

title: Swamp Cooler Cover by Brand and Model
seoTitle: Swamp Cooler Cover Size Chart by Brand & Model
description: Find cover dimensions for Portacool, Hessaire, MasterCool, and Champion evaporative coolers in inches and centimeters, then confirm the installed unit before requesting a custom quote.

sections.heading: How to Read the Size Chart
sections.body: Use the cooler's actual outside cabinet dimensions, not pad size or nominal model capacity. All dimensions below follow height × width × depth. The suggested cover dimensions include a starting fit allowance, but cabinet revisions, casters, handles, ducts, fabric, and opening layouts can change the final pattern. Measure the installed unit before ordering and send the actual dimensions without adding your own allowance.
bullets: The hem cinches at the base; added height provides fitting ease rather than a loose skirt
We confirm extra clearance around casters, handles, control panels, ducts, and side openings
A flexible project MOQ is confirmed from size, material, features, quantity, packing, and destination

sectionLinks.label: Request a confirmed pattern and quote

sections.heading: Portacool APEX Cover Sizes
sections.body: APEX model numbers identify the series, not the cabinet size or airflow. These portable units commonly need caster, handle, or hose clearance; tell us whether the cover should stop above the wheels or extend toward the floor.

sections.heading: Hessaire Portable Cover Sizes
sections.body: Hessaire listings may present length, width, and depth in different orders. The table normalizes them to height × width × depth. Confirm the orientation and measure the unit because some retailers publish different depths for the same series.
bullets: For MC26A, confirm which published dimension is the height
Some MC37 retailers list 17 in depth; if yours measures 17 in, the starting cover depth becomes 18.6 in / 47.2 cm

sections.heading: MasterCool Portable and Window Sizes
sections.body: For a window-mounted MCP44 or MCP59, measure only the outdoor portion if that is the section being covered. Do not automatically use the full product depth.

sections.heading: MasterCool Fixed-Installation Sizes
sections.body: ADA is down-draft, ASA is side-draft, and AUA is up-draft. Tell us the airflow direction so duct and service openings are placed on the correct face.

sections.heading: Champion Window Cover Sizes
sections.body: These dimensions cover the cabinet only and exclude the window duct. Confirm the installed outdoor depth before approving a pattern.

sections.heading: Champion Residential and Commercial Sizes
sections.body: DD models are down-draft and SD models are side-draft. Large commercial cabinets require correct airflow orientation, reinforced fastening, and a site check for ducts, disconnect boxes, or roof curbs.

sections.heading: Why Large Covers Need More Ease
sections.body: A cover for a two-meter cabinet is heavier and harder to lift than one for a small portable unit. Manufacturing tolerance, seam movement, handles, casters, and service panels also add up across a large pattern. Extra ease helps installation, but exposed covers still need straps or buckles so wind cannot work under the hem.
bullets: A zipper side opening is quick and can use a storm flap for outdoor exposure
Hook-and-loop provides frequent access but must be kept clean in dusty sites
Lace-up grommets provide adjustable closure for wind and dust
Very large or irregular patterns are confirmed before cutting

sections.heading: Configure the Cover Around Your Unit
sections.body: Choose polyester, Oxford, canvas, or vinyl-coated fabric for the climate; add openings for casters, handles, ducts, water inlets, or power cords; and select a drawstring, straps, buckles, or lace-up grommets. Logo and color options are also available. Typical production is 10–14 business days after dimensions, construction, quantity, and artwork are approved; shipping time is separate.

sectionLinks.label: Choose an inside or outside cover
Send model, measurements, quantity, and destination

sections.heading: Compatibility and Dimension Notice
sections.body: Brand names and model numbers are used only to identify compatible units. CoolerFit is an independent custom-cover manufacturer and is not affiliated with or endorsed by MasterCool, Hessaire, Champion, or Portacool. Unit dimensions are based on published specifications available in 2026 and may change; the measured installed cabinet and approved quote control the final pattern.

faqs.q: Can I submit measurements in centimeters?
faqs.a: Yes. Send centimeters, millimeters, or inches and use one measurement system consistently across the quote.

faqs.q: Can you make a cover for a model that is not listed?
faqs.a: Yes, subject to the confirmed project MOQ. Send outside height, width, and depth, quantity, photos, destination, and notes about protrusions or openings.

faqs.q: Should I add extra size to my measurements?
faqs.a: No. Send the actual maximum outside cabinet dimensions. We add the controlled fit allowance when the pattern is prepared.

faqs.q: Do portable cooler heights include casters?
faqs.a: Published heights often include wheels, but listings vary. Measure the installed unit and state whether the cover should stop above the casters or extend toward the floor.

intro: Use the chart to identify a starting pattern, then measure the installed cabinet before requesting a quote. Different model years, retailers, and installation hardware can change the outside dimensions even when the model name is the same.
